title: api-gateway: tune streaming proxy buffers, routing rules, and payload size limits to improve streaming stability and tool-calls (OpenAI compat)
author: Maya Chen
body:
Context: We observed intermittent streaming stalls and message truncation for large function/tool-calling payloads when requests are routed through the API gateway streaming proxy. This has impacted both Redwood-hosted and OpenAI-compat flows (notably tool/function calls with structured JSON outputs). Motivation: improve streaming stability, prevent premature buffer flush/truncation, and ensure routing rules do not inadvertently route large tool-calls to incompatible backends. Summary of changes: - Introduce adaptive proxy buffer sizing based on upstream negotiated chunking and content-type (text/event-stream vs application/json streams). - Add per-route payload_size_limit and enforce OpenAI-compat default caps while allowing tenant overrides via config. - Strengthen routing rules: prefer low-latency routables for streaming and automatically fall back to dedicated non-streaming endpoints for very large payloads. - Ensure tool/function calling payloads are validated for structured output size before forwarding and return a 413 with guidance when above configured limit. - Add instrumentation (metrics/traces) around buffer occupancy, backpressure events, and route fallback decisions. - Update OpenAI compatibility adapter to preserve chunk boundaries for function-calling responses and to surface structured-output truncation warnings in the wire protocol. - Checklist: [x] Unit tests for buffer sizing logic [x] Integration tests for streaming tool-calls across gateway routes [x] Docs: add guidance to openai-compat.md and runtime tuning docs [x] Load test pass (internal benchmark): 99.95th latency for 1k token streams improved by ~18%

Commits summary: - Refactor: move proxy buffer config into routing layer (config.go) - Perf: adaptive buffer sizing and backpressure handling (proxy.go) - Fix: enforce openai-compatible payload limits and structured-output preservation (adapter.go) - Test: integration tests for streaming tool-calls and large payload regression (streaming_tool_calls.test) - Docs: update openai compatibility guidance and example configs

Files changed (high level): - go/pkg/gateway/proxy.go: adaptive buffer sizing, backpressure hooks, improved logging - go/pkg/gateway/routing.go: new route selection heuristics for streaming vs bulk paths - go/pkg/gateway/config.go: add route.payload_size_limit and proxy.buffer defaults - go/internal/openai_compat/adapter.go: preserve chunk boundaries, add truncation warnings, respect payload limits - js/sdk/streaming.ts: client-side backpressure guidance and error mapping for 413/stream truncation - docs/api/openai-compat.md: add section about payload limits and streaming tool-calls - tests/integration/streaming_tool_calls.test: new e2e coverage - charts/gateway/values.yaml: helm defaults for buffer sizing and payload caps

Review conversation (selected): - Jordan Smith: "Can you add a small unit around the buffer growth heuristic when clients send very small initial chunks?" Maya Chen (author): "Added tests and constrained growth to a double cap; included notes in comments."

- Priya Nair: "Routing changes look good; how will this affect Dedicated routing policies that pin models to pools?" Maya Chen: "Routing prefers pinned pools when latency SLOs are required; for large streaming payloads we now optionally route to non-streaming bulk endpoints only when the route explicitly allows fallback. Dedicated clusters will continue to honor pinning unless users enable fallback in their route config. Added a note in config.go and docs."

- Omar Haddad: "Please add metric names and labels for buffer_occupancy so we can alert on sustained high occupancy rather than relying on request latency alone." Maya Chen: "Added gateway.buffer_occupancy gauge with labels {route, model, cluster, env}. Also added trace spans for fallback decision."

CI notes: - Unit tests: pass - Integration tests: pass (streaming_tool_calls.test added) - Lint: pass - E2E canary run: previously failing on canary-3, now stable after buffer cap tweak. All checks green.

Rollout plan: - Canary rollout to 10% of traffic in region us-west-2 (2/22) - Monitor buffer_occupancy, stream_truncation_count, and route_fallback_rate for 72h - If stable, ramp to 50% then 100% over 48h. Feature toggle: gateway.routing.streaming_buffer_adaptive (default: enabled)

Release notes: - Improved streaming stability and reduced stream truncation for long tool/function-calling responses. - Enforced configurable payload size limits with clearer 413 guidance for clients. - Added metrics for buffer occupancy and fallback routing decisions. - OpenAI-compat adapter preserves chunk boundaries for structured outputs.
